summary: test_checkpoint_help_documents_apply_vs_pop fails in CI due to argparse terminal-width wrapping. The test asserts 'git stash pop' as an exact substring of --help stdout, but argparse wraps long epilog lines at ~80 chars when run without a TTY (subprocess capture_output=True). At certain terminal widths the string is split as 'git stash\npop', causing the assertion to fail. Confirmed: 1 failed in local pytest run.
evidence: pytest output: 'AssertionError: assert "git stash pop" in "...`git stash\npop`..."'. The help text in scripts/azoth_checkpoint.py lines 89-90 is correct; the fragility is in the test assertion, not the script. CI runs without a TTY so argparse uses default width.
recommended_action: Normalize whitespace before asserting: use re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', r.stdout) before the in-checks, or assert the individual words 'git stash' and 'pop' appear in the text. Alternatively wrap the epilog text so the phrase fits within 72 chars regardless of terminal width.

summary: TRUST_CONTRACT §1 documents entropy caps as 'per turn' limits (files_modified ≤ 10 per turn, lines_changed ≤ 500 per turn). The hook implementation accumulates these session-scoped and resets only on session_id change. This is strictly tighter than the contract states, but the semantic gap between 'per turn' (document) and 'per session' (code) will confuse readers consulting the contract for authoritative limits. Decision ref: D2 (kernel immutability / single source of truth).
evidence: kernel/TRUST_CONTRACT.md table header: 'per turn'. entropy_check.py module docstring: 'Accumulation is *session-scoped*: counters and cumulative_entropy_delta align to scope-gate.json session_id'. The two are inconsistent; the code comment acknowledges the divergence but the contract is not updated.
recommended_action: Update TRUST_CONTRACT §1 table and narrative to say 'per session (scoped to scope-gate session_id)' instead of 'per turn'. Requires human gate (kernel file). Alternatively add a §1 footnote explaining the mechanical enforcement semantics.

summary: CI ruff step lints only 5 specific files (architecture_proposal_validate.py, kernel-integrity.py, and 3 test files). Running 'ruff check scripts/ tests/' reveals 20 errors across 13 additional files (scripts/version-bump.py, scripts/welcome.py, and 11 test files). New hook files and scripts added in this PR (edit_pretooluse_orchestrator.py, entropy_check.py, scope_gate_core.py, session_telemetry.py, alignment_summary_gate.py, entropy_state.py) are not linted by CI at all.
evidence: 'ruff check scripts/ tests/' → 'Found 20 errors.' in 13 files outside the CI whitelist. Files not covered include: test_inbox.py, test_auto_router.py, test_azoth_deploy.py, test_deliver_full_subagent_gates.py, test_l2_evidence_append.py, test_pipeline_presets.py, test_stage_summary_schema.py, test_version_bump.py, test_roadmap_dashboard.py, test_welcome.py, scripts/version-bump.py, scripts/welcome.py.
recommended_action: Expand the CI ruff step to 'ruff check scripts/ tests/ .claude/hooks/' (or 'ruff check .') so all Python files are covered. Fix the pre-existing 20 ruff errors or add per-file ignores to make the broader check green. Decision ref: D2 (quality gates).

summary: No CI step validates that azoth-deploy parity artifacts (.github/agents/, .github/prompts/, .opencode/agents/, .opencode/commands/) are in sync with their Claude source files (.claude/agents/, .claude/commands/). The new trust hook layer (P5-002 through P5-007) adds significant orchestration but parity surfaces for Copilot and OpenCode remain unverified in CI. A stale deploy silently diverges.
evidence: ci.yml has no 'azoth-deploy --dry-run' or diff check step. scripts/azoth-deploy.py supports '--dry-run' flag. .github/agents/ contains 10 agent files; no CI validates they match .claude/agents/ sources after any commit.
recommended_action: Add a CI step: 'python3 scripts/azoth-deploy.py --dry-run 2>&1 | tee /tmp/deploy-dry.txt && diff <(python3 scripts/azoth-deploy.py --dry-run 2>/dev/null) /dev/null' or compare deployed file hashes vs. a freshly generated set. Alternatively run deploy and assert no git diff in parity paths. Decision ref: D21 (platform parity).

summary: _parse_checksum_lines can insert an empty-string key into the expected checksums dict when parsing a malformed line like '<64-hex> *' (digest followed by asterisk only). After lstrip('*').strip() the path becomes ''. This empty key will never match any CHECKSUM_REL path, so no false-pass occurs, but the malformed line is silently accepted rather than flagged. A tampered checksums file could use this to obscure real entries.
evidence: Verified in REPL: line='a'*64+' *' → parts=['a'*64, '*'] → path_part='*'.lstrip('*').strip() = '' → key='' added to dict. The downstream check iterates CHECKSUM_REL and finds no match for '', so the actual kernel file falls through to 'no checksum entry' error. No false-pass, but silent ingestion of malformed input.
recommended_action: Add 'if not key: continue' guard after computing key in _parse_checksum_lines. Add a test for the empty-path edge case in tests/test_kernel_integrity.py.

summary: The SessionStart hook entry uses matcher 'startup|resume'. Claude Code's SessionStart hook fires on every new session start; the 'matcher' field for lifecycle events like SessionStart is not documented to support OR patterns in the same way as tool-name matchers. If Claude Code evaluates the matcher literally against an event type string that is neither 'startup' nor 'resume', the hook may silently not fire on legitimate session events (e.g., 'start').
evidence: .claude/settings.json: {"matcher": "startup|resume", "hooks": [...]} under SessionStart. No documentation in CLAUDE.md, kernel/GOVERNANCE.md, or official Claude Code docs confirms 'startup' and 'resume' as valid SessionStart matcher tokens. The hook has not been mechanically verified to fire on session resume.
recommended_action: Verify the valid matcher values for SessionStart events in Claude Code. If the hook should fire on all session starts, use an empty matcher '' or a wildcard. Add a comment or test documenting the expected trigger condition. Decision ref: D46 (hook specification parity).
